_comment: Hand-checked corrections applied on top of the mendeleev package values. Each entry names the source consulted on 2026-11-18. null means: no reliable measured value, so none is shown.

electronegativity._source: Pauling scale as tabulated in the CRC Handbook / WebElements (read via Wikipedia 'Electronegativities of the elements (data page)'). Values for Am-No (1.3) are estimates carried in that table.

density._source: Gases: g/cm3 at 0 C and 101.325 kPa (PubChem periodic table, cross-read with Wikipedia 'Densities of the elements (data page)': values agree to about 0.5%). Solids: mendeleev package, checked against the same page for Am, Bk, Cf, Es. No source was found for Fr and Z>=100: left empty.

melt_K._source: CRC Handbook / Lange values as listed on Wikipedia 'Melting points of the elements (data page)'. Helium does not freeze at atmospheric pressure; carbon sublimes at atmospheric pressure; the transfermium and Fr/At values are estimates, so they are left empty.

boil_K._source: CRC Handbook / Lange values as listed on Wikipedia 'Boiling points of the elements (data page)'. Estimates and lower bounds are left empty.

discovered._source: Wikipedia 'Timeline of chemical element discoveries' (first reported year); mendeleev package value where not listed here. Dates of discovery are partly a matter of definition: see discovered_note.
27: Georg Brandt showed the blue colour of cobalt glass came from a new metal.
39: Johan Gadolin found yttrium oxide in a mineral; the metal was isolated later.
60: Mosander found 'didymium' in 1841, which was a mixture; Carl Auer von Welsbach separated it into neodymium and praseodymium in 1885 (Wikipedia 'Neodymium').
86: Rutherford and Owens found the gas; Dorn's isotope gave radon its name.
91: Fajans and Goehring found a short-lived isotope; Hahn and Meitner found the longer-lived Pa-231 in 1918.
113: Detected in Russia in 2003 and at RIKEN (Japan) in 2004; recognised in 2015.
104: Claimed in Russia in 1964 and at Berkeley in 1969.
105: Claimed in Russia in 1968 and at Berkeley in 1970.
2: Seen in the Sun's spectrum in 1868 (Janssen, Lockyer); isolated on Earth in 1895 (Ramsay).
9: Isolated by Moissan in 1886; fluorspar and its acid were known earlier.
100: Formed in the Ivy Mike thermonuclear test on 1 November 1952 and identified in December 1952 (Ghiorso and colleagues); kept secret until 1955 (Wikipedia 'Fermium').
30: Zinc ores were used to make brass since antiquity, but the metal itself was recognised in India by about 1300 and isolated in Europe by Marggraf in 1746 (Wikipedia 'Zinc'); 'antiquity' here refers to its use in brass.

radius_atomic_pm._source: Wikipedia 'Atomic radii of the elements (data page)': the empirical (Slater 1964) column has no value for the noble gases; the He 120 and Ne 160 entries there are marked 'citation needed' and Ar 71 is a calculated (Clementi, Raimondi and Reinhardt 1967) value, so they are not empirical radii. Removed (null) rather than shown under the wrong label. Kr and Xe have none.

category._source: Po is a post-transition ('poor') metal: its summary calls it a radioactive metal and it is metallic in the solid (Wikipedia 'Polonium'); mendeleev lists it as a metalloid.

covalent_note._source: Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832, as tabulated on Wikipedia 'Covalent radius' (single-bond column): Mn l.s. 139 / h.s. 161, Fe 132 / 152, Co 126 / 150, C sp3 76 / sp2 73 / sp 69 pm. mendeleev stores one number per element, an average or one choice.
covalent_note.6: Cordero's radius depends on the bonding: sp³ 76 pm, sp² 73 pm (the value shown), sp 69 pm.
covalent_note.25: Cordero lists 139 pm (low-spin) and 161 pm (high-spin); the value shown is their average.
covalent_note.26: Cordero lists 132 pm (low-spin) and 152 pm (high-spin); the value shown is their average.
covalent_note.27: Cordero lists 126 pm (low-spin) and 150 pm (high-spin); the value shown is their average.

density_note._source: Wikipedia 'Densities of the elements (data page)' marks the astatine value with a question mark: no macroscopic sample exists.
density_note.85: estimate: no sample large enough to measure
